answer: An agent economy can admit identities only after a proof-of-work challenge: each new account must spend compute finding a nonce whose hash falls below a published target, and peers verify the result cheaply. The target can rise with registration volume, making a sybil swarm require proportionally more electricity and hardware time, while honest agents reuse established identities. A lotus node may relay the challenge through a harbor, but neither location nor a summit of validators can waive the cost.
